title: Alonso calls on Chelsea players to step up in Joao Pedro's absence
subtitle: Chelsea will be without Joao Pedro for their Premier League clash with Leeds United, placing more pressure on their other attackers.
paragraphs: Xabi Alonso has called on his Chelsea players to step up in front of goal in the absence of the injured Joao Pedro.
Joao Pedro has missed Chelsea's last four games across all competitions, including three in the Premier League, after suffering a thigh injury.
The Blues have failed to score in two of those three league games without the Brazilian, losing to Tottenham and Sunderland either side of a win over Manchester United.

Three of Chelsea’s four Premier League defeats this season have come to nil, and without Joao Pedro playing. The Blues average 1.8 goals per league game with him in the starting XI since the start of last season, compared to 0.9 goals without him starting.
Joao Pedro has scored five goals and provided three assists in six league games this season, more than any other Chelsea player.

Only Erling Haaland and Evanilson (both nine) have directly contributed to more goals than Joao Pedro in the English top-flight this season, but Alonso does not want to use his striker's injury as an excuse for his side.
"[We need] the whole team for that," Alonso said. "It's not just the strikers that can score. We can score from set-pieces, from defenders, from midfielders.
"It's teamwork. For sure, Joao is an important player, but we need to deal with this time without him. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.
"We need to deal with it. It's not that I'm going to look for one explanation. I think that there are more explanations for one defeat than missing just one player.
"If we do more things right, we could compete better and win at Sunderland, but there are a few things that had to be done. We want Joao Pedro back but I don't want to make a big thing out of that."
Joao Pedro has been ruled out for Chelsea's Premier League clash with Leeds United on Saturday.

Chelsea have won eight of their last 10 home games against Leeds in all competitions (D2) since a 2-0 loss in December 1999. They have already beaten the Whites 6-3 at Stamford Bridge in the EFL Cup this season.
